messages:
alex: Heads-up—product asked for role-scoped routing priorities + per-role quota overrides so enterprise customers can pin traffic to dedicated pools. Sketch in my head: roles get an optional routing_rules array with priority/intended_model/capacity_tier. Thoughts?
maria: +1 from PM side. Need console affordance to show which role is driving routing decisions and an easy way to preview effective route for a tenant. Should be visible in role detail page. :eyes: 
sam: API/data-model debate: do we attach routing_rules to the Role resource or create a separate RoleRoutingPolicy object? Pros: embedding is simpler for UI rollouts. Cons: harder to share policies between roles. 
jordan: Runtime concern—embedding is easiest for fast lookups; we evaluate policies at auth time and want minimal joins. But duplication could be bad if many roles share the same rule set. Could use an indirection (policy_id) inside Role that references a policy object. 
nina: Telemetry ask: we need per-request tags: route_evaluated=true, policy_id, role_id, policy_hit(boolean). Then dashboard can show which role/policy caused a traffic path. Also surfaces quota enforcement events. 
sam: API sketch: ```PATCH /v1/roles/{id} { "routing_rules": [{ "priority":10, "model_prefix":"redwood/gpt-4x", "capacity_tier":"dedicated", "policy_id":null }], "quota_override":{"tokens_per_minute":50000} }``` Not final, but starting point. 
maria: UX: console should not show raw rules by default. Two views: compact (effective route + quota) and advanced (full rule list + conflict preview). Also provide a simulator: input tenant attributes -> show chosen route. 
jordan: Rollout/ops: we must support canary for routing policies. Example: policy weight 10% to new pool. That implies routing_rules need support for weights and fallback order. 
nina: Security note: policy changes can redirect data to different isolation tiers. Need audit trail and require enterprise approvals/AAD sign-off for cross-tier policy edits. 
sam: Implementation idea: keep Role.route_ref -> RoleRoutingPolicy resource with fields: rules[], weights[], scope_expression. Role stores route_ref and quota_override. Advantages: role object stays small, policies are first-class and can be versioned and rolled out. 
maria: For console flows, show current policy version and allow canary rollout UI: set percent, preview affected tenants, start/stop. Also telemetry should expose policy_version in traces. 
alex: Agree with role->policy indirection. Action items: Sam to draft API PR for RoleRoutingPolicy schema + migration plan; Jordan to add runtime fast-path for policy lookup; Nina to list telemetry metrics/events; Maria to mock console compact/advanced views and canary UX. Can we have a brief F2F sync tomorrow? :calendar: 
sam: I'll put a draft PR up by EOD. Will include migration script: existing inline rules moved to a generated policy per-role. 
jordan: I'll prototype lookup cache change; want to ensure policy_version in trace spans. 
nina: I'll add metric names: `policy.eval.count`, `policy.hit.count`, `policy.fallback.count`, `quota.enforce.count`, and a tag `policy_version`. Also note retention policy for enterprise telemetry. 
deploy-bot: Canary job queued: canary-policy-validator v0.3 started for branch sam/routing-policy. Logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/ci/1234 :rocket: 
maria: Nice. One more UX ask: in role list view, show an icon if role has non-default routing/quota so admins can scan quickly. 
alex: Solid. If nobody objects, we'll move forward with indirection approach. :thumbsup:
